name: Limited-Speed Motorcycle
description: A moped or motor scooter that can go faster than 32 km/h but no faster than 70 km/h; an electric one qualifies by carrying the federal compliance label that identifies it as a limited-speed motorcycle. Outside the rules naming it, it's a motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle able to exceed 32 km/h within 1.6 km of a standing start, with a top speed of 70 km/h or less, a seat at least 650 mm high, wheel rims at least 250 mm and a wheelbase of at least 1,016 mm
Qualifies with an engine of 50 cc or less, or, if built since September 1, 1988, with the manufacturer's federal compliance label identifying it as a limited-speed motorcycle (LSM/MVL)
Riders must be 16 or older with a class M licence
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 37(1); O. Reg. 340/94, s. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Passing the road tests on one limits the licence to limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds (the L condition), and an M2-L rider may use only roads with a speed limit of 80 km/h or less
Must be registered and plated, and carry liability insurance
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 7(1); Compulsory Automobile Insurance Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.25, s. 2(1)

restrictions.rule: Every rider must wear a motorcycle helmet with the chin strap fastened
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 104(1)

restrictions.rule: Not allowed on the 400-series highways, the Queen Elizabeth Way or the other controlled-access highways listed in Regulation 630
